submission.justification: Simulated 100 GeV electron resolution (100k events each): F2 is best across the scanned thicknesses (2 mm 3.69%, 3 mm 3.60%, 5 mm 3.14%, 7 mm 3.27%, 10 mm 4.33%), so 5 mm is the optimum in the tested range. F3 reaches 4.06% at 5 mm and F1 5.26% at 5 mm. The 2025 study agrees on the ranking. Readout and mechanics are common to all candidates, so they do not affect the choice. The residual dose-rate constraint (<= 20 uSv/h at 1 m after one week of cooldown) is a hard requirement, but no document or tool provides activation or dose data for any absorber, so I could not verify it for F2. This recommendation is conditional: the dose rate for F2 at 5 mm must be confirmed (e.g., activation calculation) before adoption. If F2 fails, the next-best option is F3 (about 4.1% at 5 mm), which also needs a dose check.

requirements.requirement: Best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: F2 at 5 mm gives 3.14%, the lowest among all simulated configurations (F3 best 4.06%, F1 5.26%). Optimum between 3 and 7 mm checked.
